title: How to Tell if an Egg Is Bad: Reliable Signs and the Float Test

seo.title: How to Tell if an Egg Is Bad
seo.meta_description: A rotten odor after cracking is the clearest spoilage sign. Learn what the float test really means and how freshness differs from safety.
seo.search_intent: Recognize egg spoilage and understand the water-float test.

excerpt: A spoiled egg usually gives itself away with a strong unpleasant odor after cracking. The float test mainly indicates age because the air cell grows over time; it does not certify safety.
content_html:
You drop an egg into a glass of water and it floats. The internet's usual verdict is immediate: “bad egg.” But the test does not actually tell you that. Floating mainly tells you the egg is older, because its air cell has grown; it is not a safety test.

The clearest household sign of genuine spoilage usually appears after cracking the egg: a strong, unpleasant odor. Freshness, spoilage and microbiological safety are different questions, and separating them makes the common egg tests much easier to understand.

What the main signs actually mean

SignMeaning
Rotten or strongly off odor after crackingDiscard
Clearly abnormal appearanceMay indicate spoilage
Cracked or leaking shellHigher contamination concern
Egg floats in waterLarger air cell and older age
Thin, runny whiteLower freshness, not automatically spoilage

Smell is the most direct spoilage clue

A spoiled egg develops a characteristic unpleasant odor whether raw or cooked. If you are unsure about an older egg, crack it into a small separate bowl before adding it to batter, a skillet or other eggs.

There is no reason to taste it. A clearly bad smell is enough reason to throw it away.

What the float test is really measuring

As an egg ages, moisture and gases escape through the shell and the internal air cell grows. That changes buoyancy.

  • Sinks and lies flat: usually fresher.
  • Sinks but stands upright: older.
  • Floats: has a larger air cell and is older still.

USDA notes that a floating egg can still be usable. The test does not detect Salmonella or other pathogens. The reverse matters too: an egg that sinks is not certified pathogen-free.

A runny white usually tells you about age, not rot

Fresh egg whites tend to be thicker and the yolk sits higher. As the egg ages, the white becomes more fluid and spreads farther in a pan.

That can affect cooking quality — for example, how neatly a fried egg holds together — but it is not automatically a sign of dangerous spoilage.

Yolk color is not a freshness gauge

A deep orange yolk does not prove the egg is fresher, and a pale yolk is not a spoilage sign. Color depends mainly on pigments in the hen's diet.

Blood spots are usually less dramatic than they look

A small blood spot can result from a tiny ruptured vessel during egg formation. It does not mean the egg is fertilized or rotten and can be removed for appearance if desired.

The shell deserves more attention

An intact shell is a protective barrier. An egg that has been cracked and leaking for an unknown amount of time creates more opportunity for contamination than one you crack immediately before cooking.

Can a normal-smelling egg contain Salmonella?

Yes. Pathogens do not have to produce a detectable odor. Storage, handling and cooking still matter even when the egg looks and smells normal.

Refrigerator storage in the U.S.

USDA recommends refrigerating shell eggs and lists a typical refrigerator storage time of 3–5 weeks from purchase. Hard-cooked eggs keep about 1 week.

A simple way to check an egg you are unsure about

  1. Check that the shell is intact.
  2. Crack the egg into a separate small bowl.
  3. Look for a clearly abnormal appearance.
  4. If there is a strong off odor, discard it.
  5. If it appears normal, use it within appropriate storage and cooking practices.

What is worth remembering

Smell after cracking is a spoilage clue; floating is an age clue. An older floating egg may still be usable, and a sinking egg is not guaranteed safe. That distinction keeps a popular kitchen trick useful without asking it to do a job it cannot do.

faq.question: If an egg floats, is it bad?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Floating means the air cell has grown with age. Crack it into a separate bowl and check odor and appearance.

faq.question: How does a bad egg smell?
faq.answer: A spoiled egg develops a strong unpleasant odor that is usually obvious once cracked.

faq.question: How long do eggs keep in the refrigerator?
faq.answer: USDA lists 3–5 weeks for raw shell eggs in the refrigerator and about 1 week for hard-cooked eggs.
